5 Claude prompts. No surprises. Swipe ▸

slides.title: Notes into *clear lines*
slides.prompt: Here are my notes for a [job] for [customer]: [paste notes]. Turn them into a quote with one line per item: labor, each material with how many, any fees, then the total. Plain words a customer gets on the first read.
slides.why: One lump sum makes people wonder what they are paying for. Lines answer that before they ask.

slides.title: Say what is *not included*
slides.prompt: Here is my quote for [job]: [paste]. List 3 to 5 things a customer might think are included but are not, like [cleanup, paint, permits]. Write each as one short line for a Not included section.
slides.why: Unclear scope is a common cause of price fights after the job. One short list heads most of them off.

slides.title: Give it an *end date*
slides.prompt: Add one line to this quote saying the price is good until [date], and one plain sentence on why: my material costs can change. Friendly, not pushy.
slides.why: With no end date, a yes months later can lock in an old price. Many shops use 14 to 30 days.

slides.title: Spell out *how they pay*
slides.prompt: Write the payment terms for this quote in 3 short lines: a deposit of [amount] to book the date, the rest due [when], and how they can pay: [methods].
slides.why: If it is not written down, people pay on their own schedule and you cover the costs meanwhile.

slides.title: Read it like *the customer*
slides.prompt: Read this quote as if you were my customer: [paste]. List every question you would text me after reading it. Then rewrite the unclear lines so those questions are already answered.
slides.why: Every question the quote answers is one less text before they say yes.
